brief: The canvas displays a rotating three-dimensional molecular model of a DNA double helix. The structure is composed of labeled spheres representing the nitrogenous bases: Adenine, Thymine, Cytosine, and Guanine. The helix is constantly animated, allowing the viewer to observe the bases interacting. Key complementary base pairs—such as A with T, and C with G—will be shown moving toward each other. When the bases align correctly, temporary, visible bonds will dynamically form and break, illustrating the process of hydrogen bonding. No user input is required to observe this molecular simulation.

statement: This sketch renders a three-dimensional animated DNA double helix using p5.js's WEBGL renderer. The structure consists of labeled spheres representing nitrogenous bases (A, T, C, G) arranged in a helical pattern with complementary base pairing logic. As the helix rotates, bases from opposite strands approach each other and temporarily form hydrogen bonds when properly aligned. These dynamic bonds are visualized as connecting lines that fade out over time, simulating molecular interactions. The animation runs continuously without user input, demonstrating how genetic information is encoded through base-pairing rules in a visually engaging way.
